# Tech Team Draft: getting started

Setup only. The shared sections live in the weekly **tech-team-draft** skill and are not repeated here: Rules, Player pool seed, Goal expansion, Presets, Search query templates, Weekly pool refresh, Weekly starter picking, Lineup state, Highlights, Ideas rules, Weekly run, and Recap rendering (including the board canvas spec). Load the tech-team-draft skill and follow those sections exactly. If it is not installed, say so and stop.

## Setup-only rules
- Read-only on X: only the built-in read-only `x` tools that the tech-team-draft skill allows. Never post, reply, like, repost, follow, bookmark or DM.
- Every handle comes from the tech-team-draft skill's pool seed. Never add one from memory.
- Never ask for anything personal: no name, employer, location, contact details, relatives or account details. The goal question is the only question about the user's work, and it is about the team's work, not the person.

## Setup steps
1. Draft board: one get_users_by_usernames call for the 29 pool handles with user.fields description,name,username,profile_image_url,public_metrics,most_recent_tweet_id. This same response is Call 1 of the first recap (save it; don't call again). Show numbered tiles 1 to 29 in pool order per the tech-team-draft skill's board canvas spec, kicker `TECH TEAM DRAFT · DRAFT BOARD (setup preview)`: avatar fetched at runtime (initials for `initials` players or on fetch error), name, @handle, FOUNDER tag only where that skill's pool seed has bio evidence still in the current bio, `INACTIVE` tag for no post in the last 30 days. Markdown numbered list if rendering fails.
2. Offer the 2 presets from the tech-team-draft skill as one-tap rosters with their tile numbers, after checking their evidence against the live bios and their activity (an inactive member is shown `INACTIVE` with a suggested tweak).
3. The user picks one of: a preset name; numbers like "1, 4, 7, 9, 12" then optional "bench 2, 15"; or a tweak on a preset written `out 3 in 12` (tile 3 leaves, tile 12 takes its slot). Echo every tweak before applying it, exactly `Out: 3 @<handle> · In: 12 @<handle> (starter slot). Confirm?` (or `bench slot`), and apply only after a yes. Older wording such as "swap 3 for 12" is not accepted: reply `Say it as: out <tile> in <tile>, e.g. out 3 in 12.` Refuse 6+ starters, 7+ bench, duplicates, a tile already on the roster, an out tile not on the roster, and numbers outside the board; show the error and ask again.
4. Re-render the board with STARTER/BENCH tags for the confirmed picks and show it (tech-team-draft board canvas spec).
5. Save the working pool (a copy of the seed) and the roster as `roster_setup` in the lineup state defined by the tech-team-draft skill (same memory key or state file).
6. Ask one question: "What's your team working on?" (one line, max 120 chars), with 3 to 5 tap-to-use goal suggestions under it, short generic work topics only (for example: fine tuning performance, agent reliability, shipping faster, developer tools, eval quality), never anything personal. Suggestions are setup-only: the weekly card's footer prompt never repeats them. Save the answer as the goal. Blank is fine: ideas then use "your own work".
7. First recap now, before scheduling: do the tech-team-draft skill's weekly run steps once (read-only calls only, reusing the board response as Call 1; first run, so no pool drops), using the confirmed roster exactly, inactive starters included and tagged `INACTIVE` (no picking or swaps at setup; swap line `Lineup changes this week: none (setup roster)`), save it with run `setup`, and show it with the kicker `TECH TEAM DRAFT · <week label> (setup preview)`. The goal is expanded per the Goal expansion section and the `Terms:` line and the footer goal prompt show as on any recap; there is no picking at setup, so no fills and no banner.
8. Suggest Sunday 8:00am in the user's timezone. Create the weekly routine for the tech-team-draft skill at that time, PAUSED. Only a plain yes ("yes", "ok", "sure") turns it on. Another time replaces the default and is still created paused.

## Don't
- Don't post, like, follow or DM anyone on X.
- Don't add a handle that isn't in the tech-team-draft pool seed.
- Don't give a preset or tile a role its bio evidence doesn't back.
- Don't turn the routine on without a yes.

# Tech Team Draft (weekly recap)

First-run setup is the tech-team-draft-getting-started skill. This skill is the weekly run.

## Rules
- Read-only. Use only Grok Bot's built-in read-only `x` tools: get_users_by_usernames, get_users_posts, search_posts_all. No other X tool, no user-connected X account.
- Never post, reply, like, repost, follow, bookmark or DM. The recap goes only back to the user in chat.
- Never invent handles, bios, posts, links or numbers. Every name, quote, like count and post count comes from this run's X responses. Zero posts: `quiet week`. Handle not found: `no data`.
- Quotes are verbatim, 20 words or fewer, each linked to https://x.com/<handle>/status/<id>.
- Roster: exactly 5 starters, bench 0 to 6, 11 max, no duplicates, every handle from the working pool (seed table below plus refresh adds).
- This skill is self-contained: everything it needs is in this file. It needs no other files. State lives only in your memory or the one state file you create (see Lineup state).

## Player pool seed (29 handles, order = tile numbers 1 to 29)

Flags: `initials` = show initials, not the avatar (official/logo accounts). `former` = bio says previously at xAI. `no-bio-affil` = bio does not state the affiliation. `no-fill` = never picked as a fill (very high-volume accounts whose activity would crowd out everyone else); the player still starts when on-topic. FOUNDER = the public X bio says founder/co-founder/founding team (quoted); no other player gets the tag.

## Weekly pool refresh (each Sunday, before picking starters)
The pool table above is the seed. The working pool lives in your own memory or in a file you create (the `pool` field of the lineup state); on first run, copy the seed. Refresh it every Sunday before picking starters:
1. Find up to 3 new candidates with one read-only search_posts_all for the last 7 days, query exactly `<GOAL_OR> (SpaceX OR xAI OR SpaceXAI OR SpaceXSI) -is:retweet -is:reply -is:quote -has:cashtags`, max_results 25 (the most one call returns), expansions author_id, user.fields description,username,name,protected,most_recent_tweet_id,profile_image_url. Add an author only if all hold: public (not protected), not already in the pool, their bio shows a SpaceX or xAI affiliation, and they posted on the goal this week (an on-topic post per the picking rules; "bot" alone does not count). No affiliation evidence in the bio means no add, however popular the post.
   - Affiliation counts only as an @mention (`@SpaceX`, `@SpaceXAI`, `@SpaceXSI`, `@xAI`, any case) or a work phrase naming one of them (`at @SpaceXAI`, `building @…`, `engineer at …`, `engineering at …`, `working at …`, `designing …`, `researcher at …`). A bare word ("SpaceX fan", "I love xAI") is not affiliation.
   - Never add a ticker, maxi or investor bio, even with a mention: reject any bio with a cashtag (`$SPCX`, `$TSLA`, ...), `maxi`, `investor` or `shareholder`. Example: a bio "SpaceX, Tesla maxi ... $SPCX alpha" (like @spcxGOD) is rejected. Rank by on-topic post count, then likes; take at most 3.
2. Drop players with no post in the last 30 days, judged from `most_recent_tweet_id` in this week's get_users_by_usernames call (post time = (id >> 22) + 1288834974657 ms). Never drop one of last week's starters or bench players. On the first run (no week entry yet) skip drops entirely, and also while the state has only a setup entry (no `weekly` entry yet): drops start with the second weekly-or-later run, after the first `weekly` entry exists. Missing activity data is never a drop. Re-run: a re-run replaces that week's entry and starts the refresh again from that entry's `pool_start` (the working pool before the replaced run), and drops apply again exactly as they did on the first run of that week (the entry being replaced never counts as the newest entry).
3. Never over 35: adds stop when the pool reaches 35. Refill: while the pool is under 29, re-add retired seed players (seed order) whose `most_recent_tweet_id` in this week's lookup is within 30 days; they get their old tile numbers back and show as `+@handle` on the Pool line. Call 1 therefore looks up the working pool plus any retired seed players (one batch).
4. Empty or failed search: the pool stays exactly as it was this week (no adds, no drops). Empty goal: skip the search (no adds); drops and refill still apply.
5. Budget: the refresh uses at most 2 X calls. Fetch page 2 (the next_token page) only when page 1 returned a next_token, at least one page-1 author has a SpaceX or xAI affiliation in their bio, fewer than 3 candidates qualified after applying the add rules to page 1, and the pool is under 35. Page 1 with zero affiliated authors means stop. Otherwise stop after page 1. Bios come from the search expansions; activity comes from the weekly user lookup, so no extra calls.
6. New players get the next tile numbers; dropped players' numbers are retired. New players get no FOUNDER tag unless their bio says founder, co-founder or founding team.
7. Add one recap line under the swap line, exactly: `Pool: +@a, +@b · −@c` (adds, then drops after ` · `; omit a side that is empty), or `Pool: no changes`. If the line would pass the 984px text width, list as many entries as fit, then `+N more`.

## Search query templates
- `<GOAL_OR>` = every query form of every goal word (see Goal stems in the picking rules), then every expanded term's query form (see Goal expansion), joined with OR, in parentheses, no blind plurals. For shift, template, worker: `(shift OR shifts OR template OR templates OR worker OR workers)`. For grow, brand: `(grow OR grows OR brand OR brands)`. For honing, moonshotting: `(hone OR honing OR moonshot OR moonshots OR moonshotting)`. For fine tuning, performance: `("fine tune" OR "fine-tune" OR finetune OR "fine tuning" OR "fine-tuning" OR finetuning OR performance OR performances)`; with its expanded terms that becomes `("fine tune" OR "fine-tune" OR finetune OR "fine tuning" OR "fine-tuning" OR finetuning OR performance OR performances OR lora OR eval OR latency OR benchmark OR inference)` (fine-tune is already covered by the compound, so it adds no form).
- Prefetch query: `<GOAL_OR> (from:h1 OR from:h2 OR ...) -is:retweet -is:reply` over the working-pool handles in pool order, max_results 25 (the most one call returns). If a chunk returns a next_token, do not page: the starters' own posts (weekly run steps 5 and 7) are still fetched in full. 29 from: terms come to about 600 chars, so split: fill chunk 1 with handles in pool order and start a new chunk at the first handle that would push the full query (goal part, from: group and suffix) past 512 chars. For the 29-handle seed and the goal "building Grok Bot templates for shift workers" that split falls before @lingxi (tile 25), giving 2 queries. Every handle appears in exactly one chunk; logo accounts are included (their posts are read, they just are not auto-picked). That split example is for the goal words alone; expanded terms lengthen `<GOAL_OR>`, so chunks are cut earlier. Prefetch is at most 3 chunks: if the split would need more, remove expanded-term forms from the query, last term first, until it fits in 3 (removed terms still count for on-topic matching).
- Widened prefetch: the same chunks and queries over the last 14 days instead of 7 (only when step 2 of Goal expansion calls for it).
- Activity sweep query (only for fills): `(from:h1 OR from:h2 OR ...) -is:retweet -is:reply` over the fill-eligible players (see Picking rules 4) not already starting, in pool order, split at 512 chars the same way (at most 3 chunks), always over this week only (the last 7 days, even after the lookback widens), max_results 25, expansions author_id, post.fields created_at,public_metrics. No pagination. Coverage: the sweep covers the week only if every chunk returned without a next_token and none failed; otherwise its counts are partial and are not used (see the fill fallback in Picking rules 4).
- Never send a query without `-is:retweet -is:reply`.

## Goal expansion (each run, before judging posts)
The root fix for thin weeks: widen what counts as on-topic before any filling.
1. Expand: before judging any post, expand the goal into 5 to 8 related terms, capped at 8 (never more than 8, never fewer than 5). Terms are short technical words or phrases a builder would actually write about that goal, not generic words (the generic list in the picking rules applies) and not handles. Example: "fine tuning performance" adds fine-tune, LoRA, eval, latency, benchmark, inference. Each term matches posts by the Goal stems rules (a term is treated like a goal word; matching is case-insensitive) and adds one query form to `<GOAL_OR>`: the term lowercased, in quotes if it has a space or hyphen, no added forms, skipped when a goal word already covers it. Expanded terms count for on-topic matching, the refresh search, the prefetch and the ideas' goal-word rule. Save them on the week entry (`terms`) and show them on the card (the `Terms:` line). Empty goal: no expansion, no `Terms:` line.
2. Widen: if fewer than 5 pickable players have an on-topic post in the last 7 days, run the widened prefetch (last 14 days) and judge again. The lookback for this run (`lookback`: 7 or 14) then also applies to the starters' post fetches, post counts and highlights, and the `Terms:` line ends with ` · 14-day lookback`.
3. Fill: only after both steps, if on-topic pickable players are still under 5, fill the open spots per the picking rules (most active, marked `fill: most active, off-goal`).

## Presets (2)
Each member's evidence is a verbatim string from their public X bio. Before offering a preset, check each evidence string is still in that player's current bio (case-insensitive) and the handle is in the pool; drop a preset whose starters no longer all check out. Also check activity: a member with no post in the last 30 days (from `most_recent_tweet_id`) is offered tagged `INACTIVE`, with a suggested `out <tile> in <tile>` tweak to an active pool player.

## Weekly starter picking (from the goal)
1. Goal words: lowercase the goal, drop possessive 's, take words of 3+ letters (a hyphenated word such as fine-tuning is one word, never split), fold a trailing plural s (words over 3 letters), and drop generic words: grok, bot, bots, how, why, when, where, who, can, should, get, with, that, this, from, your, their, team, work, working, what, and, the, for, building, build, builds, making, make, about, into, some, more, lots, a, an. Example: "building Grok Bot templates for shift workers" gives shift, template, worker; "how do we grow the brand" gives grow, brand ("grow" is a real goal word, never generic).
   Goal stems (one per goal word, used for matching and for `<GOAL_OR>`):
   - Base form: if the word ends in -ing, drop it and undo a doubled final b, d, g, m, n, p or t (moonshotting -> moonshot); else if it ends in -ed, drop it the same way; strip a suffix only when 3+ letters remain (need stays need). If what remains is 3 letters ending consonant-vowel-consonant (last letter not w, x or y), add back the e (honing -> hone, coding -> code).
   - Stem: the base minus a trailing -e (template -> templat, hone -> hon).
   - Stem of 4+ letters: a post word matches when it starts with the stem at a word boundary and the rest of the word is empty or a known suffix: e, s, es, d, ed, ing, er, ers, th, ly, ment, ments, ness, ion, ions, or a doubled final consonant plus ing, ed, er or ers (ting, ted, ...). So moonshot matches moonshots, moonshotting; grow matches grows, growing, growth, but not growl. Query forms: the base, base + s, and the original goal word if different (moonshot, moonshots, moonshotting).
   - Stem under 4 letters: no prefix match and no added forms (no -s, -ed, -d or -ing). Match exact whole words only: the base and the original goal word (honing gives hone, honing; fine gives fine, so fines and fined do not match; app gives app). Those are also the query forms.
   - Compounds: a hyphenated goal word, or two adjacent goal words that are also commonly written hyphenated or as one word, is one term (fine tuning is one term; ordinary pairs such as shift workers stay separate words). Take its base and stem from the closed form with the rules above (finetuning -> finetun), so it always gets the 4+ letter prefix match, and the join in a post may be a space, a hyphen or nothing: fine-tuning, fine tuning, finetune, finetuning and fine-tuned all match. Query forms (these replace base + s): for the last part's base and for the original goal word, the spaced and hyphenated forms (in quotes) and the closed form (`"fine tune" OR "fine-tune" OR finetune OR "fine tuning" OR "fine-tuning" OR finetuning`).
   - Examples: "how do we grow the brand" gives goal words grow, brand, stems grow, brand. "Honing and moonshotting my team" gives goal words honing, moonshotting ("and", "team" generic, "my" under 3 letters), stems hon (short: hone, honing) and moonshot (prefix). "fine tuning performance" gives goal words fine tuning (one compound term) and performance, stems finetun (compound, prefix) and performanc. "building Grok Bot templates for shift workers" gives stems shift, templat, worker.
   Empty goal: no goal words and no expanded terms, so skip every goal-dependent search (pool refresh search, prefetch and widened prefetch); all 5 starters are marked fills from the activity sweep. The empty-goal rules win over the zero on-topic week rules and the thin-week rules: no banner, no `Terms:` line, and exactly 3+3 ideas for "your own work".
2. On-topic post = an original post (not a reply, not a repost) within this run's lookback window whose text matches a goal stem or an expanded term per the Goal stems rule (prefix match for stems of 4+ letters, exact forms for short stems). A post that only says "bot" is not on-topic. A search match alone is not on-topic: X can match on a link, a handle or an expanded URL, so re-check every returned post's own text (with t.co links removed) against the goal stems before counting it, for prefetch, refresh and posts calls alike.
3. Only pickable players are ranked: every pool player except `initials` accounts (official/logo accounts such as @grok, @bot, @SpaceXSI, @cursor_ai). Logo accounts stay on the board and the user can hand-pick them at setup (by number or preset tweak); a hand-picked one is on the setup roster only (weekly runs draft fresh, so it is never carried into a weekly lineup). They are never auto-picked as starters, fills or bench. Rank pickable players with 1+ on-topic posts by: on-topic post count (high first), then total likes on those on-topic posts (engagement tie-break), then pool number.
4. Weekly reset: every weekly run drafts a fresh 5 from this week's on-topic players only. Last week's starters are never carried over; one starts again only by being on-topic this week (or by being picked as a fill). 5 or more on-topic: top 5 start (mode on-topic). 0 to 4 on-topic (after Goal expansion and the widened lookback): they start, and the open spots are filled from the fill-eligible players not already starting. Fill-eligible = pickable (never an `initials`/logo account), not flagged `no-fill` (such as @elonmusk), and not a fill in both of the last 2 saved weekly entries (read each entry's `fills` list; a missing list counts as none; a re-run ignores the entry it replaces). So nobody is a fill more than 2 weeks in a row. Rank fills by this week's post count in the activity sweep (originals in the last 7 days), then total likes on those posts, then pool number; players with no post in the last 30 days come last. If the sweep does not cover the week (a chunk returned a next_token or failed), do not use its counts: take fill-eligible players with a post in the last 30 days in pool order, then the rest in pool order. Only if fewer fill-eligible players remain than open spots, lift the 2-weeks-in-a-row rule (pool order); logo and `no-fill` accounts are never fills. Every fill is marked `fill: most active, off-goal` on its card (mode thin), and the card shows the top banner `Thin week: N on-topic players` (`Thin week: 1 on-topic player` when N = 1, `Thin week: 0 on-topic players` when none). Empty goal: no on-topic players, so all 5 are fills (mode thin, no banner: the empty-goal rules win). There is no filled or fallback mode and no carryover mode. Setup run (`setup`): no picking at all; starters and bench are exactly the just-confirmed `roster_setup` (mode setup), and the swap line is `Lineup changes this week: none (setup roster)`.
   Inactive players (weekly runs): a fresh draft never needs a slot replacement, since on-topic players have a post in the window and fills are ranked by activity. A player with no post in the last 30 days (from `most_recent_tweet_id` in Call 1) starts only if nothing else can fill the 5. Setup runs keep the confirmed roster and only mark such starters `INACTIVE`.
5. Never an empty or short lineup: the fill ranking ends in pool order (with the 2-in-a-row lift as the last resort), so it always reaches 5, and every fill is marked. Never an unmarked fill: a starter without an on-topic post this week is always a marked fill.
6. Bench = this week's on-topic pickable players not starting (ranked), max 6; anyone past 6 goes back to the pool. No carryover: last week's starters and bench players are never carried onto this week's bench; they return to the pool unless they are on-topic (bench) or starting this week. A thin week therefore has an empty bench (0 to 6 holds). Setup runs: bench = the confirmed roster_setup bench.
7. Recap rows: the BENCH row shows exactly this week's bench (0 to 6). A separate POOL row shows the rest of the working pool (not starting, not bench, no `initials`/logo accounts) in pool order, as many as fit on one line, then `+N more`.
8. Swap line, exactly: `Lineup changes this week: in @a, @b · out @c, @d`, or `Lineup changes this week: none`. It compares this week's starters against the last saved `weekly` entry (a re-run ignores the entry it replaces). Week 1 (no saved `weekly` entry yet, only setup): compare against the setup roster (`roster_setup` starters) and write `Lineup changes since setup: in @a · out @c` or `Lineup changes since setup: none`; the setup entry stays and the weekly entry is appended. If a swap line would pass the 984px text width, list as many handles as fit, then `+N more` (same rule as the Pool line), keeping the `in` and `out` labels: cut the longer side first, e.g. `in @a, @b +2 more · out @c +3 more`.

## Lineup state
Keep all state in your own memory under the key `tech-team-draft`, or in a file you create in your own data folder at `tech-team-draft/state.json`. Use one of the two, the same one every week. Shape: `{"pool": [...], "roster_setup": {"preset", "starters", "bench"}, "goal": "...", "weeks": [{"week", "run", "label", "goal", "terms", "lookback", "starters", "fills", "bench", "mode", "on_topic", "swap", "pool", "pool_start"}]}` (`fills` = the starters marked as fills, `on_topic` = the count shown in the banner; `fills` is stored on every weekly entry, `[]` when there are none, because the 2-in-a-row fill rule reads it). `run` is `setup` (the first recap at setup) or `weekly`. Saving: if the newest entry has the same week id and both it and this run are `weekly`, replace it (a re-run); otherwise append a new entry, so a setup entry and that week's Sunday run are both kept. Re-run: a re-run replaces that week's entry (it does not append), and drops apply again (see Weekly pool refresh). Last week's lineup (for the swap line and drop protection) is the last saved `weekly` entry before this run; with none, use roster_setup. It never seeds this week's starters or bench (weekly reset).
- Goal change: the newest goal the user gave wins. Save it to `goal` right away, and every run stores the goal it used on that week's entry (`weeks[].goal`). A re-run after a goal change replaces that week's entry with the new goal. The card footer asks `Reply with next week's goal, or I'll keep: <goal>`: a reply is a goal change for the next run; no reply keeps the goal. Nothing waits on a reply and the run never asks for the goal at run time (no new setting).
- Week id: the date of the Sunday that ends the run date's Monday-to-Sunday week, in the user's timezone, as `YYYY-MM-DD`. A Thursday Oct 15 2026 setup and the Sunday Oct 18 2026 run both get `2026-10-18` (the setup entry is kept and the Sunday entry is appended after it). Do not use ISO week numbers.
- Week label (shown on the recap): `WEEK OF <MON> <D> <YYYY>` for the first day of the 7-day window, uppercase month (a Sunday Oct 18 2026 run is `WEEK OF OCT 11 2026`).

## Highlights
- "This week" in the highlight and post-count rules means this run's lookback window (7 days, or 14 after widening). A fill's highlight is their most-liked post (it is off-goal).
- A starter's highlight is their most-liked on-topic post this week, from their own posts or from this week's prefetch results; if they have no on-topic post, their most-liked post. Ties: the newest post.
- Excerpt: first remove every t.co link (`https://t.co/...`), then strip emoji, then take the first 20 words verbatim (links never use a word slot), and end with `…` when the post was longer. Link https://x.com/<handle>/status/<id>. Zero posts: `quiet week`, no highlight.

## Ideas rules
- Count only on-topic highlights. 3 or more on-topic starters: exactly 3 sharper ideas (small, doable this week) and 3 stretch ideas (bigger). 1 or 2 on-topic starters: ideas only from those highlights, at most 1 sharper and 1 stretch each, no padding from off-topic posts.
- Each idea is one short line tied to one real highlight from this week: it names that player as @handle and uses a goal word (any word that matches a goal stem or an expanded term per the Goal stems rule). A fill's off-goal highlight backs an idea only under the zero on-topic week rule below or on an empty goal. "bot" alone never counts as on-topic, since it is a generic word.
- Reuse: a highlight may back at most 2 ideas, one sharper and one stretch; never two ideas in the same group from one highlight. Prefer 6 different highlights when there are 6.
- Zero on-topic week (no starter has an on-topic highlight): the top banner reads `Thin week: 0 on-topic players` (there is no separate line under the Pool line), and give only ideas that quote or paraphrase the highlight post itself and use a goal word: 0 to 3 sharper and 0 to 3 stretch. If none fits honestly, give 0 ideas. Never force 3+3 that week. With 0 ideas, the IDEAS block is the label `IDEAS` followed by the line `No on-topic posts this week`.
- Empty goal: ideas are for "your own work" and need no goal word.
- No idea from a quiet or not-found player. No facts beyond the quoted posts.
- Before showing, check: 3+3 (fewer on a week with 0 to 2 on-topic starters, as above), each ref has a highlight, each names its @handle, each uses a goal word, reuse limit held. Fix and re-check on any miss.

## Weekly run (up to 25 X calls)
1. Load the lineup state (memory or the state file). Check the roster against the Rules; stop on any error. Compute the week id and label. A re-run of a saved week replaces that entry.
2. Goal expansion step 1: expand the goal into 5 to 8 terms (no X call) and build `<GOAL_OR>`.
3. Call 1: get_users_by_usernames with all working-pool handles plus any retired seed players in one batch, user.fields description,name,username,public_metrics,profile_image_url,most_recent_tweet_id. Keep each user's numeric `id`.
4. Pool refresh per the refresh rules (max 2 calls). Save `pool_start`, the new pool and its `Pool:` line.
5. Prefetch (max 3 calls): the prefetch query chunks per the search query templates, last 7 days, expansions author_id, post.fields created_at,public_metrics,in_reply_to_user_id. No pagination. Re-check each post's own text against the goal stems and expanded terms.
6. Goal expansion step 2: under 5 on-topic pickable players, run the widened prefetch (last 14 days, max 3 calls) and judge again.
7. Goal expansion step 3: still under 5, run the activity sweep over this week (max 3 calls) and rank fill-eligible players (no logo, no `no-fill`, no 3rd fill in a row; pool order if the sweep does not cover the week).
8. Pick this week's starters fresh with the picking rules (weekly reset: on-topic first, then marked fills), then the bench, record the lineup state and build the swap line against the last saved weekly entry (setup roster in week 1).
9. Fetch get_users_posts for each of this week's 5 starters, so every starter has a full window of posts.
   Every get_users_posts fetch: `id` = the numeric user id from Call 1 (not the handle), start_time 7 days ago (14 when widened), end_time now, max_results 25 (the most one call returns), exclude replies,retweets, post.fields created_at,public_metrics. If the response has a next_token, fetch the next page (at most 2 pages per player). The count is exact only when the window is covered: the last page has no next_token and either returned fewer than 15 posts or its oldest post is within a day of start_time (X can drop filtered posts from a full page without giving a token). Otherwise show `N+ posts` with N = posts received.
10. Highlights per the highlight rules; ideas by the ideas rules.
11. Render the recap per the rendering spec; markdown card if rendering fails.

## Call math
1 user lookup + up to 2 refresh + up to 3 prefetch + up to 3 widened prefetch + up to 3 activity sweep + 5 starters x up to 2 pages = 22 max, under a 30 per run budget. Usually 1 + 1 + 2 + 5 = about 9 to 15 (the widened prefetch and the sweep run only on thin weeks). On a 429, wait for x-rate-limit-reset, retry that call once, then mark the player `no data`.

## Setup
First-run setup (draft board, presets, picks, tweaks, goal question, first recap, paused schedule) is the **tech-team-draft-getting-started** skill, which ships with this one. If there is no lineup state yet, run that skill first. Everything the weekly run needs is in this file.
